speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked	the Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) what is the number of Islamic religious teachers in Singapore who are registered under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) since it started; (b) whether the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) or the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) has conducted an engagement with religious teachers who are not registered with ARS to understand the reasons or barriers to their registration; (c) whether the accreditation levels are benchmarked to an internationally recognised body; (d) whether PERGAS is the right entity to spearhead the mandatory registration of asatizahs given that MUIS will have no control over their membership and leadership; (e) whether the mandatory registration of asatizahs requires an amendment to the Administration of Muslim Law Act; and (f) what is the development plan for ARS going forward.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is an inclusive system that recognises asatizahs from various schools of thought, so long as they meet the standards and training requirements set by the Asatizah Recognition Board (ARB), which comprises senior asatizahs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This training requirement is part of a larger Continuous Professional Education (CPE) programme for our asatizahs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The courses within the CPE programme support the professional development of our asatizahs and help update them on contemporary issues and challenges related to the socio-religious life of our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Through this, our ARS asatizahs are better equipped to serve and retain the confidence of the community.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS, PERGAS and ARB have been working hand in hand to strengthen the ARS to ensure that our asatizahs have the appropriate qualifications and training, anchored in our multiracial and multi-religious context.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The idea of having a mandatory ARS is not new.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In fact, it was proposed by senior asatizahs more than a decade ago but our focus at that time was on developing a suite of quality ARS programmes to benefit our asatizahs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is important that our asatizahs have recognised these benefits for themselves and see the value of ARS.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Now, with the asatizah fraternity's strong support and the calls from community leaders for mandatory ARS, the time is right to strengthen ARS further.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: ARS does not consist only of PERGAS alone.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Rather, ARS is a joint effort by MUIS, PERGAS and ARB.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MUIS, together with PERGAS and ARB, will continue to engage the relevant stakeholders on the implementation of mandatory ARS, including our religious and community leaders, Malay/Muslim organisations, and private Islamic education centres, in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With their support, ARS will continue to evolve to serve the needs of our community.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some private madrasahs engage teachers who are not formally trained to be asatizahs to teach in their respective madrasahs.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would these teachers be required to register themselves as well?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: My second supplementary question is: what offence would a non-ARS registered person be committing if found teaching religious education to the public, especially those in private settings, such as homes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If they have teachers who have been teaching but who do not meet ARS requirements, we will work with them to draw up a transition plan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As mentioned in my reply, we want to be as inclusive as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Yet, at the same time, we must also educate the public on which teachers are to be engaged and also which should not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, the list of ARS teachers is already made available online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We hope that parents who want to run home classes will engage those who are already on the list.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I want to know whether ARS will apply to non-Singaporean religious teachers, especially for those who are invited to Singapore to give sermons and speeches on Islam?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If not, then how do we ensure that they maintain the same standards as the ARS-registered teachers?
